what_its_for: This antibiotic is used to treat urinary tract infections (UTIs) — infections in your bladder or urinary system caused by bacteria. It works by killing the bacteria causing your infection. It is only for bladder/urinary infections and will NOT work for infections in other parts of your body.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth WITH food or milk. This is very important — taking it with food helps your body absorb the medicine better AND helps prevent an upset stomach. Swallow the capsule whole. Do not crush or chew it. Drink plenty of water and fluids throughout the day while taking this medicine. Take every dose exactly as your doctor prescribed, and finish ALL of the medicine even if you feel better before it is gone. Stopping too early may allow the infection to come back.
dosing: The usual adult dose for treating a UTI is one 100 mg capsule taken twice a day (every 12 hours) for 5 to 7 days, or as directed by your doctor. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions. Do not take more or less than prescribed. For prevention of repeat UTIs, your doctor may prescribe a lower dose taken once daily — follow those specific directions carefully.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do NOT double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the capsules away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store in your bathroom. Keep the bottle tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of leftover medication.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids that contain magnesium (such as Maalox or Mylanta) at the same time as nitrofurantoin, as they can reduce how well this medicine works — separate them by at least 2 hours. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine, as it may increase the risk of side effects. Do not take this medicine if you are also taking certain other antibiotics like fluoroquinolones (such as ciprofloxacin) unless your doctor approves, as they may interfere with each other. Avoid prolonged exposure to sunlight, as this medicine may make your skin more sensitive to the sun — use sunscreen if going outdoors.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you experience any of the following: trouble breathing, shortness of breath, or a new cough (may be a sign of a rare but serious lung reaction); yellowing of your skin or eyes, or dark urine (signs of liver problems); severe skin rash, blistering, or peeling; numbness or tingling in your hands or feet (nerve damage); persistent nausea, vomiting, or stomach pain; signs of a severe allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or dizziness. Also call your doctor if your symptoms do not improve within 2 to 3 days, or if they get worse. Note: Your urine may turn dark yellow or brownish in color — this is harmless and normal with this medicine.
when_it_works: Most people start to feel better within 1 to 3 days of starting treatment. However, it is very important that you finish the entire course of antibiotics even if you feel completely better. Stopping early can allow bacteria to survive and cause the infection to return, possibly with bacteria that are harder to treat.
special_populations: Pregnancy: This medicine should NOT be used at 38 to 42 weeks of pregnancy (near the end of pregnancy) or during labor and delivery, as it may harm the newborn. Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: This medicine passes into breast milk and should not be used if you are breastfeeding an infant under 1 month old. Ask your doctor before breastfeeding. Elderly (age 65 and older): Older adults may be at higher risk for serious side effects, including lung and liver problems. Your doctor should carefully weigh the benefits and risks before prescribing this medicine to older patients, especially for long-term use. Kidney problems: This medicine is NOT recommended if you have significantly reduced kidney function (creatinine clearance below 30 mL/min), as it will not work properly and can build up to harmful levels in your body. Children: This medicine should NOT be given to infants under 1 month of age.
